title: Form Controls
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of form controls and when it is appropriate.
Apply text inputs using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check email and password inputs and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study form controls and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Form Controls should guide users through a form rather than merely decorate controls. Associate labels and help text with fields, preserve native semantics, and validate submitted data on the server as well as in the browser.

content_blocks.text: Use the pinned Bootstrap 5.3.x baseline, follow the official component documentation, and verify semantic HTML, responsive behavior, and keyboard access before reusing the pattern.

content.task: Add form controls to a short form. Associate every field with help or error text as needed and test an invalid submission.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating form controls as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
